newsitem.title: UK: Mideast dirty tankers flat but softer tone.
newsitem.headline: Mideast dirty tankers flat but softer tone.

text.p: Middle East and Mediterranean dirty tanker rates were flat but with a slightly softer tone on Thursday, brokers said.

Med 80,000 tonne rates, which have soared since mid-January, were little changed at W150-160, but an Italian broker said there was sufficient tonnage available and the market could dip from its recent highs.
The 130,000 tonne Med market was quiet, with vessels continuing to be fixed at about W95.
In the Middle East a London broker said rates were easing slightly on a lack of fresh enquiry.

Mideast/west voyages eased to W52.5 from W55 for very large crude carriers (VLCCs), with trips to Japan steady at W65 and to Singapore at W52.5. "The market is weakening slightly. There isn't much life in it," the broker said.

The transatlantic sector also dipped, with 130,000 tonne ships down to W90/92.5 from W95. "There's plenty of interest in Suezmaxes in other sectors like West Africa and the Caribbean...This is putting owners a bit in command (on transatlantic routes)," another broker said.
Transatlantic VLCCs were steady at W62.5, as were these vessels on West Africa/U.S. Gulf trips.
Inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonne vessels were softer at W105/107.5 against around W117.5 on Wednesday on a lack of cargoes, brokers said.
In contrast, fuel oil edged up, with inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne cargoes fixed at W205 against W195 and cross-Med at W190 against W180.
"From an owners' point of view things are looking positive. In the Baltic and cross-UKC there isn't that much tonnage available, especially for prompt ships," a fuel oil broker said.
In the U.S., brokers said they saw some softening on good availability of tonnage in the Caribbean.
They put 70,000 tonnes Caribs/U.S. Gulf at W160/165, down from W165, while 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were steady at about W175. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
